newsitem.title: USA: Conn. utility sees nuke restart in '97.
newsitem.headline: Conn. utility sees nuke restart in '97.

text.p: Northeast Nuclear Energy Co. said Tuesday it expected to be ready to restart one of its three troubled Millstone nuclear power plants in the third quarter of 1997.

The two remaining Millstone units at the Waterford, Conn., nuclear facility could resume producing power in the fourth quarter of 1997 and the first quarter of 1998, respectively, pending regulatory approval, the company said.
Northeast Nuclear officials, who also refer to the company as NU Nuclear, met with federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) officials.
The three Millstone units, which have an overall rated generating capacity of nearly 2,700 megawatts, have been shut since March due to safety concerns raised by the NRC.
"An essential part of these restart plans is that we fundamentally change the way NU Nuclear operates," said company President Bruce Kenyon.

"And that entails four basic things: Setting the proper standards, improving our ability to find and correct problems, building a track record of meeting regulatory commitments and establishing a satisfactory employee concerns environment," he said.
Kenyon gave no details on the likely order that the three units might be brought back into service, but said unit 1 had "the most aggressive schedule."
Unit 1, opened in 1970 and rated at 660 megawatts, is the oldest and smallest of the three power plants.
Kenyon said shortly after he joined the company in September that Northeast expected to have at least one of the three plants reopened in the second half of 1997.
Kenyon joined the company during a massive restructuring aimed at addressing the problems plaguing Millstone.

Hartford-based Northeast Utilities, NU Nuclear Energy's parent company, last month warned in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that maintaining and upgrading the facility and the cost of replacement power could result in a fourth-quarter loss.
